🚀 Data Engineering: From Source to Insights — 25 Concepts Every Data Engineer Should Know
As Data Engineers, we work with many tools and technologies, but the fundamentals remain the same: move, store, transform, orchestrate, validate, and serve data.
I created this visual guide to break down 25 important Data Engineering concepts into simple, interview-friendly explanations. 👇
🔹 1. Moving Data
01️⃣ Data Ingestion
02️⃣ Batch Processing
03️⃣ Stream Processing
04️⃣ Change Data Capture (CDC)
05️⃣ Full vs Incremental Loads
🔹 2. Storing Data
06️⃣ Database
07️⃣ Data Lake
08️⃣ Data Warehouse
09️⃣ Lakehouse
🔟 Partitioning
🔹 3. Transforming Data
1️⃣1️⃣ ETL

1️⃣4️⃣ Aggregations

🔹 4. Running Pipelines
1️⃣6️⃣ Orchestration
1️⃣7️⃣ DAG
1️⃣8️⃣ Dependencies
1️⃣9️⃣ Retry

🔹 5. Trusting Data
2️⃣1️⃣ Data Quality
2️⃣2️⃣ Schema Validation
2️⃣3️⃣ Data Freshness
2️⃣4️⃣ Data Lineage
2️⃣5️⃣ Idempotency
💡 One important lesson:
Knowing individual tools is not enough. A strong Data Engineer should understand how data flows end-to-end and why each component is used.
For example:
Source → Ingestion → Storage → Transformation → Orchestration → Data Quality → Serving
These concepts are also extremely useful when preparing for Data Engineering interviews involving SQL, Snowflake, DBT, Azure, AWS, Databricks, PySpark and modern data platforms.
